+# Issue #6061 — T0 finite control fixture
+
+## H / T / D / C / U
+
+**H.** On a frozen finite target family, prediction-error-triggered action chunks preserve terminal target-tracking effect and release safety at least as well as fixed-period feedback while reducing full observations on predictable motion; abrupt reversal tests whether the residual trigger recovers sooner than nonpredictive sample-and-hold.
+
+**T.** Eight opaque fixture rows × four policies (`fixed`, `triggered`, `sample_hold`, `yield`), six action ticks, max speed 1, capture period 4, residual trigger threshold 1. The fixture includes constant/perfect-predictor, abrupt reversal/stale-predictor, target disappearance, lease invalidation, focus invalidation, target-binding loss, stationary/zero-error, and abrupt-jump cases. Candidate output logs capture ticks, residual checks, action ticks/values, release reason, final tracking error, effect, and safety. A continuous low-cost `fast_position` stream supplies the residual; full observation is counted only at selected capture ticks. The raw-only auditor separately reconstructs all 32 policy traces and rejects five mutations (drop row, false capture, target-loss continuation, lease violation, false effect). Frozen local image intended: `python@sha256:dddfd7e07f9d15aeeca61529320492139d21cac7f0070c00609243e51e4e0016`, `--pull never --network none --cpus 1 --rm`, candidate and auditor in separate WSLc containers, source read-only, unique outputs. GPU is intentionally unused.
+
+**D.** `PASS_METHOD_SCOPED` only if all 32 rows independently reconstruct; triggered policy matches fixed policy's effect on every declared eligible row; at least one perfect-predictor row uses fewer full observations; stale-predictor reversal recovers with effect; target/focus/lease/binding gates release before any invalid action; and all five raw mutations are rejected. Any trace disagreement or safety continuation is FAIL; provenance or runtime gate failures are STOP; no retries.
+
+**C.** The fixture's deterministic residual stream and motion law are authored; the residual may be more informative than a real GUI image channel, and cost is counted as observation/probe counts rather than measured wall-clock time.
+
+**U.** Synthetic method result only. No DOOM/MAP01, GUI, model, OS input, physical held key, latency distribution, natural error rate, safety guarantee, user benefit, or runtime validation.
+
+## Local construction checkpoint (not formal)
+
+Host CPython 3.11.9 construction-only run `construction-02`: candidate/auditor agreement on 32 rows, zero errors (`PASS_METHOD_SCOPED`); five mutated outputs rejected (5/5). Candidate raw, audit output, stderr and exits are retained in the construction directory. The source is still preparation state: no current-main branch has been frozen, no formal candidate/auditor container has run, no allocation result is claimed, and the formal retry budget remains zero.
+
+Two earlier pre-freeze construction attempts were rejected and remain distinct from the formal allocation. Attempt 01 compared the post-action agent state with the next tick's target, falsely failing the perfect-predictor and stale-predictor controls. During the sensor-refactor attempt, the raw-only oracle retained one reference to the removed residual field and stopped with `KeyError`; no construction result was produced. The final pre-freeze construction corrected both conditions and saved fresh output. These were source/construction issues, not formal candidate/auditor invocations or scientific outcomes; their console errors remain in this task transcript.
+

+# Archived #6061 T0 preparation and construction, not a formal result
+
+This package preserves all 14 original files byte-for-byte from
+`research/intermittent-control-6061-t0-20261003` at
+`f236f4c0d4ae0371ef6a42fa5389072348b3436f`, formerly Draft PR #6825.
+The historical freeze status remains `PREPARED_FORMAL_INVOCATIONS_NOT_STARTED`:
+formal candidate/auditor 0/0, retries zero. The original WSLc owner/runtime
+clearance gate is retained; neither archive integration nor branch cleanup
+authorizes that allocation to start. Any future experiment needs a fresh
+current-main/source/output/image/owner check and valid bounded clearance.
+
+## Recoverable material and limitations
+
+The authored fixture has eight scenarios and four policies, 32 construction
+rows, synthetic position/residual inputs, and operation counts rather than
+measured latency. The historical Windows construction receipt reports exact
+candidate/auditor agreement and five rejected mutations. This is not a formal
+Issue result, live controller/game/GUI/model/held-key observation, user-safety
+guarantee, or performance measurement. Earlier failed construction attempts
+are described in the unchanged PLAN and construction report; their transcript
+console output is not in this remote package. The report refers to stderr
+files, but neither candidate_stderr.txt nor audit_stderr.txt is present at the
+published source tip. Recovery does not invent those missing artifacts.
+
+Both original FREEZE files are the same blob. The freeze's two
+`construction-02/...` hash labels refer to files actually published under
+`construction/02/...`; recovery tests map these labels without changing the
+original freeze. All eight declared hashes are verified. Package-local
+`-text` attributes preserve the original Windows bytes.
+
+## Local recovery gates
+
+New tests only check the archived source/freeze identities and construction
+receipt, replay the saved 32-row construction raw through the retained checker,
+and send five mutated copies of that saved construction raw to the same
+checker in temporary directories. These are offline construction-integrity

+import copy,json,subprocess,sys,tempfile

+x=copy.deepcopy(base); next(r for r in x["rows"] if r["scenario"]=="r03" and r["policy"]=="triggered")["release"]="horizon"; mutations["target_loss_continue"]=x
+x=copy.deepcopy(base); next(r for r in x["rows"] if r["scenario"]=="r04" and r["policy"]=="triggered")["actions"].append({"tick":3,"input":1.0}); mutations["lease_violation"]=x
+x=copy.deepcopy(base); next(r for r in x["rows"] if r["scenario"]=="r02" and r["policy"]=="triggered")["effect"]=False; mutations["false_effect"]=x
+results={}
+with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:

+  run=subprocess.run([sys.executable,auditor,fixture,path],capture_output=True,text=True)
+  results[n]={"rejected":run.returncode!=0,"returncode":run.returncode}
+print(json.dumps({"all_rejected":all(x["rejected"] for x in results.values()),"controls":results},sort_keys=True))
+sys.exit(0 if all(x["rejected"] for x in results.values()) else 2)"},{"sha":"4525ddcf1939a393136a1655f8d09ecd16e3fd2d","filename":"research/analysis/intermittent_control_6061_t0_20261003/run_construction.py","status":"added","additions":17,"deletions":0,"changes":17,"blob_url":"https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/blob/e74cfc78b84d286ff3faabf2696129b988655c1b/research%2Fanalysis%2Fintermittent_control_6061_t0_20261003%2Frun_construction.py","raw_url":"https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/raw/e74cfc78b84d286ff3faabf2696129b988655c1b/research%2Fanalysis%2Fintermittent_control_6061_t0_20261003%2Frun_construction.py","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/Unjuno/agent-interface/contents/research%2Fanalysis%2Fintermittent_control_6061_t0_20261003%2Frun_construction.py?ref=e74cfc78b84d286ff3faabf2696129b988655c1b","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@

+print(audit_run.stdout.strip() or audit_run.stderr.strip())
+sys.exit(audit_run.returncode)"},{"sha":"7aa3fa92cc35e2f08aafe4e66f5a3676b5d2d2d6","filename":"research/analysis/intermittent_control_6061_t0_20261003/test_archival_construction.py","status":"added","additions":72,"deletions":0,"changes":72,"blob_url":"https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/blob/e74cfc78b84d286ff3faabf2696129b988655c1b/research%2Fanalysis%2Fintermittent_control_6061_t0_20261003%2Ftest_archival_construction.py","raw_url":"https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/raw/e74cfc78b84d286ff3faabf2696129b988655c1b/research%2Fanalysis%2Fintermittent_control_6061_t0_20261003%2Ftest_archival_construction.py","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/Unjuno/agent-interface/contents/research%2Fanalysis%2Fintermittent_control_6061_t0_20261003%2Ftest_archival_construction.py?ref=e74cfc78b84d286ff3faabf2696129b988655c1b","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+"""Offline tests of saved construction raw; no candidate or container launch."""
+import copy
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+PACKAGE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+SAVED = PACKAGE / 'construction/02/candidate_raw.json'
+
+
+class ArchivedConstructionTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def check_raw(self, raw_path):
+        run = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', str(PACKAGE / 'auditor.py'), str(PACKAGE / 'fixture.json'), str(raw_path)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)
+        return run.returncode, json.loads(run.stdout)
+
+    def test_all_original_freeze_hashes_and_duplicate_freeze(self):
+        frozen = json.loads((PACKAGE / 'FREEZE.json').read_text())
+        hashes = frozen['construction_sha256']
+        self.assertEqual(len(hashes), 8)
+        for label, expected in hashes.items():
+            relative = label.replace('construction-02/', 'construction/02/', 1)
+            with self.subTest(path=label):
+                self.assertEqual(hashlib.sha256((PACKAGE / relative).read_bytes()).hexdigest(), expected.lower())
+        self.assertEqual((PACKAGE / 'FREEZE.json').read_bytes(), (PACKAGE / 'FREEZE_V1.json').read_bytes())
+
+    def test_preparation_is_not_promoted_to_formal_result(self):
+        frozen = json.loads((PACKAGE / 'FREEZE.json').read_text())
+        self.assertEqual(frozen['status'], 'PREPARED_FORMAL_INVOCATIONS_NOT_STARTED')
+        self.assertEqual((frozen['formal_candidate'], frozen['formal_auditor'], frozen['retries']), (0, 0, 0))
+        receipt = json.loads((PACKAGE / 'construction/02/mutation_stdout.json').read_text())
+        self.assertTrue(receipt['all_rejected'])
+        self.assertEqual(len(receipt['controls']), 5)
+
+    def test_saved_construction_raw_replays_exactly(self):
+        code, replayed = self.check_raw(SAVED)
+        saved_receipt = json.loads((PACKAGE / 'construction/02/audit_stdout.txt').read_text())
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
+        self.assertEqual(replayed, saved_receipt)
+        self.assertEqual(replayed, {'errors': [], 'rows': 32, 'verdict': 'PASS_METHOD_SCOPED'})
+
+    def test_five_mutated_saved_raw_copies_fail_through_checker(self):
+        saved = json.loads(SAVED.read_text())
+        mutations = {}
+        bad = copy.deepcopy(saved)
+        bad['rows'].pop()
+        mutations['drop_row'] = bad
+        for name, scenario, change in (
+            ('false_capture', 'r01', lambda row: row['capture_ticks'].append(1)),
+            ('target_loss_continue', 'r03', lambda row: row.update(release='horizon')),
+            ('lease_violation', 'r04', lambda row: row['actions'].append({'tick': 3, 'input': 1.0})),
+            ('false_effect', 'r02', lambda row: row.update(effect=False)),
+        ):
+            bad = copy.deepcopy(saved)
+            change(next(row for row in bad['rows'] if row['scenario'] == scenario and row['policy'] == 'triggered'))
+            mutations[name] = bad
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='archived-6061-construction-') as temporary:
+            for name, bad in mutations.items():
+                with self.subTest(control=name):
+                    path = Path(temporary) / (name + '.json')
+                    path.write_text(json.dumps(bad))
+                    code, receipt = self.check_raw(path)
+                    self.assertEqual(code, 1)
+                    self.assertEqual(receipt['verdict'], 'FAIL_AUDIT')
+                    self.assertTrue(receipt['errors'])
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()"}]}

+# Issue #6061 — T0 finite control fixture
+
+## H / T / D / C / U
+
+**H.** On a frozen finite target family, prediction-error-triggered action chunks preserve terminal target-tracking effect and release safety at least as well as fixed-period feedback while reducing full observations on predictable motion; abrupt reversal tests whether the residual trigger recovers sooner than nonpredictive sample-and-hold.
+
+**T.** Eight opaque fixture rows × four policies (`fixed`, `triggered`, `sample_hold`, `yield`), six action ticks, max speed 1, capture period 4, residual trigger threshold 1. The fixture includes constant/perfect-predictor, abrupt reversal/stale-predictor, target disappearance, lease invalidation, focus invalidation, target-binding loss, stationary/zero-error, and abrupt-jump cases. Candidate output logs capture ticks, residual checks, action ticks/values, release reason, final tracking error, effect, and safety. A continuous low-cost `fast_position` stream supplies the residual; full observation is counted only at selected capture ticks. The raw-only auditor separately reconstructs all 32 policy traces and rejects five mutations (drop row, false capture, target-loss continuation, lease violation, false effect). Frozen local image intended: `python@sha256:dddfd7e07f9d15aeeca61529320492139d21cac7f0070c00609243e51e4e0016`, `--pull never --network none --cpus 1 --rm`, candidate and auditor in separate WSLc containers, source read-only, unique outputs. GPU is intentionally unused.
+
+**D.** `PASS_METHOD_SCOPED` only if all 32 rows independently reconstruct; triggered policy matches fixed policy's effect on every declared eligible row; at least one perfect-predictor row uses fewer full observations; stale-predictor reversal recovers with effect; target/focus/lease/binding gates release before any invalid action; and all five raw mutations are rejected. Any trace disagreement or safety continuation is FAIL; provenance or runtime gate failures are STOP; no retries.
+
+**C.** The fixture's deterministic residual stream and motion law are authored; the residual may be more informative than a real GUI image channel, and cost is counted as observation/probe counts rather than measured wall-clock time.
+
+**U.** Synthetic method result only. No DOOM/MAP01, GUI, model, OS input, physical held key, latency distribution, natural error rate, safety guarantee, user benefit, or runtime validation.

+   if release is None: release="horizon"

+  expected[(s["id"],p)]={"scenario":s["id"],"policy":p,"capture_ticks":caps,"residual_checks":checks,"chunks":chunks,"actions":acts,"release":release,"final_agent":x,"final_target":tx,"final_error":er,"effect":bool(release=="horizon" and et==H and er<=0.5),"safe":all(s["present"][a["tick"]] and s["lease"][a["tick"]] and s["focus"][a["tick"]] and s["bound"][a["tick"]] for a in acts)}

+"""Offline tests of saved construction raw; no candidate or container launch."""
+import copy
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+
+PACKAGE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+SAVED = PACKAGE / 'construction/02/candidate_raw.json'
+
+
+class ArchivedConstructionTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def check_raw(self, raw_path):
+        run = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', str(PACKAGE / 'auditor.py'), str(PACKAGE / 'fixture.json'), str(raw_path)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)
+        return run.returncode, json.loads(run.stdout)
+
+    def test_all_original_freeze_hashes_and_duplicate_freeze(self):
+        frozen = json.loads((PACKAGE / 'FREEZE.json').read_text())
+        hashes = frozen['construction_sha256']
+        self.assertEqual(len(hashes), 8)
+        for label, expected in hashes.items():
+            relative = label.replace('construction-02/', 'construction/02/', 1)
+            with self.subTest(path=label):
+                self.assertEqual(hashlib.sha256((PACKAGE / relative).read_bytes()).hexdigest(), expected.lower())
+        self.assertEqual((PACKAGE / 'FREEZE.json').read_bytes(), (PACKAGE / 'FREEZE_V1.json').read_bytes())
+
+    def test_preparation_is_not_promoted_to_formal_result(self):
+        frozen = json.loads((PACKAGE / 'FREEZE.json').read_text())
+        self.assertEqual(frozen['status'], 'PREPARED_FORMAL_INVOCATIONS_NOT_STARTED')
+        self.assertEqual((frozen['formal_candidate'], frozen['formal_auditor'], frozen['retries']), (0, 0, 0))
+        receipt = json.loads((PACKAGE / 'construction/02/mutation_stdout.json').read_text())
+        self.assertTrue(receipt['all_rejected'])
+        self.assertEqual(len(receipt['controls']), 5)
+
+    def test_saved_construction_raw_replays_exactly(self):
+        code, replayed = self.check_raw(SAVED)
+        saved_receipt = json.loads((PACKAGE / 'construction/02/audit_stdout.txt').read_text())
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
+        self.assertEqual(replayed, saved_receipt)
+        self.assertEqual(replayed, {'errors': [], 'rows': 32, 'verdict': 'PASS_METHOD_SCOPED'})
+
+    def test_five_mutated_saved_raw_copies_fail_through_checker(self):
+        saved = json.loads(SAVED.read_text())
+        mutations = {}
+        bad = copy.deepcopy(saved)
+        bad['rows'].pop()
+        mutations['drop_row'] = bad
+        for name, scenario, change in (
+            ('false_capture', 'r01', lambda row: row['capture_ticks'].append(1)),
+            ('target_loss_continue', 'r03', lambda row: row.update(release='horizon')),
+            ('lease_violation', 'r04', lambda row: row['actions'].append({'tick': 3, 'input': 1.0})),
+            ('false_effect', 'r02', lambda row: row.update(effect=False)),
+        ):
+            bad = copy.deepcopy(saved)
+            change(next(row for row in bad['rows'] if row['scenario'] == scenario and row['policy'] == 'triggered'))
+            mutations[name] = bad
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='archived-6061-construction-') as temporary:
+            for name, bad in mutations.items():
+                with self.subTest(control=name):
+                    path = Path(temporary) / (name + '.json')
+                    path.write_text(json.dumps(bad))
+                    code, receipt = self.check_raw(path)
+                    self.assertEqual(code, 1)
+                    self.assertEqual(receipt['verdict'], 'FAIL_AUDIT')
+                    self.assertTrue(receipt['errors'])
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()"}]}

Reproduced cases falsely completed a delivery-uncertain action, lost an already completed prefix, consumed rewritten references, or turned a dispatched/held-input refusal into a pre-input refusal. Retain the validated callback values before the journal runs: keep the earlier journal/observation/admission/effect custody fixes, copy the exact outer terminal dictionary, and compute the original pre-input refusal predicate before emission. Original release/type/reference, deadline, authority and cooperative cancellation guards remain.

The terminal repair deliberately uses hook-free `dict.copy()`. Deep-copying arbitrary values before their existing validation could let a custom copy hook convert a rejected release subclass or non-string reference into an accepted value. Regression controls preserve those original rejections. This protects synchronous declared scalar values and completed/pending history; it does not authenticate physical input release or task effects, arbitrary opaque objects, or concurrent mutation.

Validation on Windows CPython3.12.14: the first v5 run reproduced five failures among72 impacted compiled tests, with zero setup errors. V6 passes72/72 in normal and optimized runs. Twenty explicitly loaded tests pass from isolated archive imports in normal and optimized modes; all12 terminal fixture records also match the source runs. First failures and raw streams remain recoverable. These are ordinary finite CPU regressions; no consumed producer/profile/allocation or peer diagnostic was replayed.

relay could accept overflowing numbers, duplicate decoded keys or deeply nested JSON before SDK entry. An independent native Windows review also found that inherited cp932 text stdin changes literal UTF-8 keys, bypassing duplicate detection and consuming an ID at SDK serialization failure.

Refuse these JSON/decode failures before ID consumption and read pipe bytes strictly as UTF-8. Preserve already decoded text callers, accepted-ID consumption, SDK uncertainty and no replay. Fifteen related regressions pass; a committed current-package SDK stream returns six planned refusal/response boundaries and closes without a backend connection. All first failures remain, including an original static-valid response after text changed under cp932, which shows why static validity alone is not transport proof.

an app-server reader survives join(timeout), close currently closes its journal and returns normally. A later valid frame then fails on the closed journal, and the proposed startup cleanup helper records a completed close and removes its exit callback.

This change checks reader.is_alive() after the join and raises TimeoutError before journal access. The journal remains open for the reader; the existing helper can record incomplete cleanup and retain its callback. Healthy close, explicit None and the existing journal mutex block retain their behavior.

Validation: first current-source RED has 3 failures out of 8; fixed ordinary and optimized selections pass 8/8 each, unchanged adopted EOF regressions pass 4/4, and a new frozen native closed/held pair verifies the actual old-helper receipt, late journal/cache row, real atexit callback retention/removal and owned terminal endpoints. The first saved-audit, packaging and publication setup failures are preserved. The 98-member inert custody manifest includes 25 literal path projections. The new regression is selected explicitly; the full native protocol catalogue and hosted CI are not claimed as tested by this new selection.

Scope: two production lines, one stdlib regression module, one index row and 100 inert archive images. No model/game/GUI/input/provider use or native/formal replay. Journal mutex, UTF8, send, EOF registration and v39 wait owners remain separate. This is a draft source proposal; main sends are zero. Own #6944 V1 adoption remains held. Exact-content nonauthor quorum and actual-current coupling/application authority remain outstanding.

Reproduced cases falsely completed a delivery-uncertain action, lost an already completed prefix, consumed rewritten references, or turned a dispatched/held-input refusal into a pre-input refusal. Retain the validated callback values before the journal runs: keep the earlier journal/observation/admission/effect custody fixes, copy the exact outer terminal dictionary, and compute the original pre-input refusal predicate before emission. Original release/type/reference, deadline, authority and cooperative cancellation guards remain.

The terminal repair deliberately uses hook-free `dict.copy()`. Deep-copying arbitrary values before their existing validation could let a custom copy hook convert a rejected release subclass or non-string reference into an accepted value. Regression controls preserve those original rejections. This protects synchronous declared scalar values and completed/pending history; it does not authenticate physical input release or task effects, arbitrary opaque objects, or concurrent mutation.

Validation on Windows CPython3.12.14: the first v5 run reproduced five failures among72 impacted compiled tests, with zero setup errors. V6 passes72/72 in normal and optimized runs. Eleven new methods cover12 complete graph/callback/return/edit/receipt-or-exception records, byte-identical across source runs. The committed builder produced a407890-byte archive, SHA256 `c1cb45f3cfb8f0107b142e97992123abd153e686686f7b9a310e242bc148be86`; all51 source blobs match the fixed Git commit, with56 archive entries. Twenty explicitly loaded tests pass from isolated archive imports in normal and optimized modes; all12 terminal fixture records also match the source runs. First failures and raw streams remain recoverable. These are ordinary finite CPU regressions; no consumed producer/profile/allocation or peer diagnostic was replayed.

Fixed v6 head `aabf685b619273592b109fbdbafaabdc0216dbdb`, tree `ce01f7e67e01c55052665898151af81d929da89a`, single parent v5 `3bd35c386171b8fbeaa892cfbb8bcac7d56bc57b`; review base `636986a804a6004cd047db7e8cc5e62c02d585d8`. Compiled source20712 bytes, SHA256 `56f36d24d9dd6120f964b5ac4cfdd0129f8b718a05c6ea842930f4af0575441a`. Whole PR191 paths: seven live code/test/doc paths plus184 unchanged inert evidence files. The new three-path delta passes the default whitespace check. Historical full-diff CRLF diagnostics remain qualified failures, with original evidence bytes preserved.

Actual nonauthor0820's [terminal evidence](https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/pull/6934#issuecomment-5968695112) and [v5 applicability](https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/pull/6934#issuecomment-5968739980) are preserved and checked as saved data; that worker's missing child PID remains unknown. The [v5 author hold](https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/pull/6934#issuecomment-5968839083) remains historical. [Prospective v6 proposal](https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/pull/6934#issuecomment-5969120851): epoch `pr-6934-compiled-callback-custody-20261003-v6-terminal-return`, digest `f4563d0e1372ce0e05b25b3047d0ac31a7590e64ee3fa1bb882f1a0d9a3faa8a`. Recoverable evidence starts at [proof part1](https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/pull/6934#issuecomment-5969124371); ordered remaining parts5969124610,5969125025,5969125366,5969125673,5969126032,5969126411,5969126722.201 records restore from the UTF-8 pool; all original/public joins and first publication-wording correction are retained. Package source pins are quoted; source bytes are reconstructible from the immutable Git commit.

APPLICATION_HOLD: the same three actual prospective nonauthors are fixed before renewed votes: `01a0ff33-df63-7d60-871f-a7ecd2649d07`, `01a0ff52-70ab-7f10-82b3-e60375a032fb`, `01a0ff58-7772-7312-9c2a-459f38d6734d`. issues.title: Separate safety control plane from planner data and telemetry paths
issues.body:
## Motivation

Recent journal-stall evidence exposed a safety-relevant ordering failure: while receipt write/flush was blocked, the probe used the same caller path for notification and cancellation. Physical/owned input release still occurred under expiry/cancel, but receipt ordering was no longer reliable. This shows that a runtime can preserve the input-side invariant while its observation/telemetry path is stalled or reordered.

The research question is whether safety-critical control should use a separate control plane from planner-facing observation, receipt persistence and event delivery.

## Core hypothesis

A minimal independent safety plane can preserve cancellation, expiry and release reachability even when the observation/telemetry/planner plane is blocked, slow, reordered or failed:

```
safety plane: authority → cancel/expiry → release → safety receipt
data plane: capture → observation → planner → ordinary receipts
```

The safety plane should have no dependency on synchronous PNG/JSON serialization, journal flush, stdout delivery or planner acknowledgement. It may emit a compact best-effort safety record after the physical action, but physical release must be governed independently.

This is stronger than “use a persistent journal”: persistence optimizes the data plane, while this proposal tests whether critical control remains live when the data plane is unavailable.

## Why existing Issues do not already cover it

- #2 identifies process-level failsafe and X11 stall risk, but does not define or test a separate control-plane architecture.
- #10 measures Python/research overhead and possible native boundaries, but does not make safety reachability independent of telemetry.
- #14 defines planner-facing interrupt retention, not the physical cancellation/release path.
- #15 links causal evidence, but assumes evidence can be recorded after the critical action; it does not guarantee action reachability during evidence failure.
- #16 concerns transactional action grouping, not emergency control-plane independence.

## Candidate design

Define two explicit paths:

1. Safety path: expiry timer, cancel owner, key/button release and authority revocation. It uses bounded, non-blocking primitives and cannot wait on journal, image encoding, planner delivery or ordinary event subscribers.
2. Data path: observations, planner replies, ordinary receipts, causal metadata and persistence. It can be buffered, degraded or marked unavailable without blocking the safety path.

Candidate safety outcomes should distinguish:

- RELEASE_REQUESTED
- RELEASE_INJECTED
- RELEASE_CONFIRMED, only when OS/backend evidence exists
- RELEASE_UNCONFIRMED
- DATA_PLANE_BLOCKED
- AUTHORITY_REVOKED

The design must not call a release “verified” merely because a timer callback ran or a log line was written.

## Safety constraints

- Safety actions remain owned by the runtime/input broker, not the planner.
- Expiry and cancellation cannot be delayed by synchronous image, JSON, stdout or filesystem operations.
- Cleanup key/button-up actions remain allowed after authority expiry; new task input does not.
- A blocked data plane must not silently grant continued authority.
- The independent path must not introduce a second conflicting input owner.
- If OS/backend confirmation is unavailable, report the uncertainty and preserve the failure artifact.
- No hard release deadline may be claimed without a measured and enforced lower-level watchdog.
- Cross-plane IDs and clock domains must allow post-hoc reconstruction without imposing synchronous ordering on the critical path.

## Smallest falsifiable experiment

Use the existing held-input/expiry/cancel fixture and compare:

A. current coupled path, with receipt write/flush/serialization blocked;
B. persistent journal but coupled cancellation;
C. independent safety path with the same blocked data-plane conditions.

Inject blocking at write, flush, stdout delivery and image/receipt serialization. Run cancellation and lease expiry during a held pointer/button or key operation. Use an independent observer to inspect physical input state and saved application effects.

Require tests for:

- release under data-plane block;
- no late motion/key-down/button-down after expiry;
- cancel/expiry precedence;
- duplicate cancel;
- blocked data path recovery;
- receipt ordering after unblocking;
- data-plane failure without loss of safety evidence.

## Metrics

Primary:

- physical release success and release-confirmation coverage;
- late task-input count after expiry/cancel;
- release overshoot under each injected stall;
- authority correctness;
- false claims of verified release;
- task/application correctness.

Secondary:

- time from cancel/expiry to release request and injection;
- data-plane outage duration tolerated;
- safety receipt completeness and ordering after recovery;
- ordinary planner/observation degradation;
- CPU, memory and implementation complexity.

## Red-team objections

- A second control plane may create races or two-owner bugs.
- Python threads are not an actual process-level safety boundary.
- X11 itself may stall, so separation cannot prove hard release guarantees.
- Safety receipts can still be lost if persistence is unavailable.
- The architecture may be equivalent to the process-level failsafe already listed in #2.
- Additional synchronization and cross-plane reconciliation may cost more than it saves.
- A release action can be physically injected but still not accepted by the OS.

The experiment must measure the observed guarantee and explicitly separate it from an unproven hard deadline.

## Promotion / rejection rule

Promote only if the independent path preserves or improves all existing release and authority correctness gates under injected data-plane stalls, with no new ownership race, and materially reduces release delay or uncertainty. Require differential tests showing identical behavior when the data plane is healthy.

Reject or defer if it cannot be separated from ordinary thread scheduling, if the X11/backend stall dominates all cases, if safety evidence becomes less auditable, or if the added path introduces any late task input or ownership violation.

## Relationship to current evidence

The latest journal-stall cohort records physical/owned release under blocked write or flush, but also retains a write/cancel receipt-ordering failure. That is the concrete trigger for this proposal. The issue does not claim that the current runtime is unsafe or that a separate control plane will solve OS-level stalls; it asks whether the dependency can be isolated and measured.

The broader safety principle is:

> Failure of observation or explanation must not prevent an already-required safety action.

This is an Agent Interface concern because the planner may be remote and slow, while input authority and release must remain correct even when the planner-facing interface is unavailable.

A journal callback could rebind a previously returned execution terminal or effect verdict after validation. Reproduced cases falsely completed a delivery-uncertain action, lost an already completed prefix, consumed rewritten references, or turned a dispatched/held-input refusal into a pre-input refusal. Retain the validated callback values before the journal runs: keep the earlier journal/observation/admission/effect custody fixes, copy the exact outer terminal dictionary, and compute the original pre-input refusal predicate before emission. Original release/type/reference, deadline, authority and cooperative cancellation guards remain.

The terminal repair deliberately uses hook-free `dict.copy()`. Deep-copying arbitrary values before their existing validation could let a custom copy hook convert a rejected release subclass or non-string reference into an accepted value. Regression controls preserve those original rejections. This protects synchronous declared scalar values and completed/pending history; it does not authenticate physical input release or task effects, arbitrary opaque objects, or concurrent mutation.

issues.title: fix(research): return app-server EOF errors without draining stderr
issues.body:
When the app-server stdout reader closes, both public wait methods synchronously drain stderr under their condition lock. A still-open stderr writer holds that failure path past the configured wait; invalid stderr bytes instead raise UnicodeDecodeError. Return AppServerError from known stdout closure, explicitly stating that stderr was not drained. Matching queued replies, notifications and journals remain intact.

[Comparison and limits](https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/blob/4f17db76d98cb2f55cb553844db7d1b9be143300/research/live_control/appserver_eof_stop_59_01a0ff51/REPORT.md): one prospectively pinned original and repaired arm, each eight actual Linux/arm64 inert children in a cached network-none OrbStack container. Original held-stderr request/notification calls remain pending with internal deadlines206.848/204.004ms overdue; repaired calls finish before the fixed checkpoint. Both healthy values survive; two invalid-stderr decoding errors become the intended error. All16 children and both drivers exit0. The driver, separately from client.close, closes the remaining owned pipes. No request replay, live Codex/model/game/GUI/input or efficiency result.

Validation: new four-method test has original RED2/healthy2, repaired4/4 on macOS normal and optimized plus4/4 in the pinned Linux image. Original saved-only reader passes16 rows/26 corruption controls; two subsequent integer-for-Boolean copies expose its equality gap. Original checker/result and first acceptances remain. A versioned saved-only repair checks the identical raw and rejects30 controls, with zero native replay. Initial sparse setup and incomplete local staging/commit are retained and repaired before first branch transmission. All158 leaf files,157 manifest targets and134 original/public custody joins are preserved; eight own-path projections distinguish public hashes from private originals.

Scope: only the two EOF diagnostic branches, new test/protocol registration and evidence/navigation. Whole-call writes, predicates, journal locks, process/descendant cleanup, actual control feedback and physical release remain unresolved. Existing #6945 diagnostic, #6952 response-cache, startup and journal-cleanup owners retain their work. Refs #59/#57; author01a0ff51-d447, FINAL-v5. Draft pending a fixed-before-votes proposal, two actual eligible existing nonauthor votes, exact current-main combination confirmation and live conditional forward application.
